rationale: Retain CAG Holdings as Carlyle's manager-level airport infrastructure platform and correct the ownership history rather than retiring it. Ferrovial acquired 96% of Carlyle's former 51% indirect interest in the New Terminal One at JFK at the June 10, 2022 financial close, leaving Carlyle with approximately 2% indirect ownership. Ferrovial's 2026 SEC materials continue to report that 2% interest, and no later Carlyle full exit or signed transfer was identified through August 19, 2026. CAG Holdings is the platform; JFK NTO LLC and The New Terminal One are the concessionaire and associated project and are not separate PortCos. The platform's precise equity percentage, legal investment date and current headquarters are not publicly disclosed, so they are not inferred.

beforeImage.name: CAG Holdings / The New Terminal One at JFK
beforeImage.description: CAG Holdings is the Carlyle-backed airport infrastructure platform associated with the New Terminal One redevelopment at John F. Kennedy International Airport. The project company develops, finances, constructs, and will operate a new international terminal serving airlines and passengers under a long-term lease and concession structure with the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. The model is asset-heavy and contract-based because returns depend on terminal infrastructure, phased construction, and long-term airport operations rather than a light-asset services model. Public project materials describe the New Terminal One as a 2.4 million-square-foot facility with 23 gates and a total project value of about $9.5 billion. Carlyle established CAG Holdings in 2019 as a dedicated airport infrastructure platform, and the JFK consortium reached financial close and full notice to proceed in 2022.

milestones.event: Carlyle identified CAG Holdings as a portfolio company of Carlyle Global Infrastructure Opportunity Fund and its dedicated U.S.-based airport infrastructure platform.
New York announced the consortium selected to develop the New Terminal One at JFK.
The New Terminal One consortium announced financial close and full notice to proceed.
Construction activity accelerated at the site as phased demolition and major works progressed.

aliases: CAG Holdings / The New Terminal One at JFK
The New Terminal One at JFK
afterImage.description: CAG Holdings is Carlyle's U.S. airport infrastructure platform associated with The New Terminal One at John F. Kennedy International Airport. The related project company, JFK NTO LLC, is developing, financing, constructing and will operate a roughly $9.5 billion, 2.6 million-square-foot international terminal with 23 gates under a long-term Port Authority lease. Carlyle originally held a 51% indirect project interest; at financial close on June 10, 2022, Ferrovial acquired 96% of that position and Carlyle retained approximately 2% indirect ownership. Ferrovial's 2026 SEC materials report the current project split as Ferrovial 49%, Carlyle 2%, JLC Infrastructure 30% and Ullico Infrastructure 19%. CAG remains the manager-level PortCo; JFK NTO LLC and the terminal are the associated project rather than separate PortCos. No later Carlyle full exit or signed divestiture was found through August 19, 2026. CAG's platform-level stake, precise legal entry date and current headquarters are not publicly disclosed.
